name: California
authority: California Secretary of State, Notary Public Section
fee_note: $20.00 per apostille. In person, a $6.00 special handling fee also applies for each different public official's signature authenticated.
mail_time: Varies. The office publishes a Current Processing Times page; mail requests are processed in the order received and cannot be pulled for expedited service.
walkin_time: Same-day service at the Sacramento and Los Angeles offices and at Apostille Pop-Up Shops.
payment: Mail: check or money order payable to Secretary of State. Sacramento counter: Visa/Mastercard, check, money order, or cash. Los Angeles counter: card, check, or money order (no cash).
addresses: USPS mail: Notary Public Section, P.O. Box 942877, Sacramento, CA 94277-0001
FedEx/UPS/DHL: Notary Public Section, 1500 11th Street, 2nd Floor, Sacramento, CA 95814
In person (Sacramento): 1500 11th Street, 3rd Floor, Sacramento, CA 95814
In person (Los Angeles): 300 South Spring Street, Room 12513, Los Angeles, CA 90013 (temporarily on the 1st floor, suite 1215, due to an elevator outage)
what_to_send: The original document signed by a California public official, or an original notarized/certified document (no photocopies)
A cover sheet naming the country where the document will be used (the office provides an Apostille Mail Request Cover Sheet)
Check or money order for $20.00 per apostille
A self-addressed return envelope (prepaid postage if you want tracking; otherwise it returns by regular USPS mail)
tips: Pop-Up Shops bring in-person apostille service to county offices around the state; check the official Pop-Up Shop page for dates.
If you are on a deadline, the office itself points you to same-day in-person service rather than mail.
summary: California apostilles are issued by the Secretary of State's Notary Public Section for $20 per apostille. You can mail your request to Sacramento, or get same-day service in person in Sacramento or Los Angeles, where a $6 special handling fee per official's signature also applies. Mail processing times vary, and the office posts its current processing dates online.

name: New York
authority: New York Department of State, Division of Licensing Services, Apostille and Authentication Unit
fee_note: $10 per document.
mail_time: Not published on the official page. Drop-off requests (Albany and NYC) are processed by receipt date, not as priority.
walkin_time: Same-day walk-in service in New York City, Albany, Binghamton, Buffalo and Utica; limited to 10 documents per customer.
payment: Fee paid with the request form; the current form requires a CVV for all credit card payments.
addresses: Mail: New York Department of State, Division of Licensing Services, Apostille and Authentication Unit, PO Box 22001, Albany, NY 12201-2001
Express carriers / Albany walk-in: 1 Commerce Plaza, 99 Washington Avenue, 6th Floor, Albany, NY 12231
NYC walk-in: 123 William St., 2nd Fl., New York, NY 10038-3804
Also walk-in: Binghamton (44 Hawley St, Room 1506), Buffalo (295 Main St, 8th Fl, Suite 821), Utica (207 Genesee St)
what_to_send: The document, already certified by a New York State official or County Clerk where required
The Apostille/Certificate of Authentication Request Form (incomplete forms are returned)
$10 per document
Optional: a prepaid overnight shipping label (labels that bill your credit card or 'bill sender' are not accepted); otherwise documents return by first-class mail
tips: Birth, death and marriage certificates issued by a local or county official must first be certified by the County Clerk of the county where issued. Records issued by the NYS Department of Health with the Director of Vital Statistics / State Registrar signature do not need County Clerk certification.
For NYC birth and death certificates, request a 'Letter of Exemplification' when ordering the record.
Notarized documents must first be certified by the County Clerk of the county where the notary is commissioned.
FBI background checks go to the U.S. Department of State, not New York.
sources: NY DOS: Obtain an Apostille/Certificate of Authentication
summary: New York apostilles come from the Department of State's Apostille and Authentication Unit and cost $10 per document. Locally issued vital records and all notarized documents must be certified by the County Clerk first. Same-day walk-in service is offered in New York City, Albany, Binghamton, Buffalo and Utica, for up to 10 documents.

name: Texas
authority: Office of the Texas Secretary of State, Authentications Unit
fee_note: $15 per document (not per page). Adoption proceedings: $10 per document, total not to exceed $100 per child (use Form 2103).
mail_time: Up to two weeks from the day of receipt, per the official page; actual times vary with volume.
walkin_time: Same-day service, max 10 documents. Walk-in Monday and Friday only; appointment required Tuesday–Thursday. Drop box for more than 10 documents: about 72 hours.
payment: Mail: check or money order drawn on a U.S. bank and payable to the Office of the Texas Secretary of State, or a funded SOS Client Account. In person: check, money order, credit/debit card, or cash (exact change only).
addresses: Mail: The Office of the Texas Secretary of State, Authentications Unit, P.O. Box 13550, Austin, TX 78711-3550
In person: Authentications Unit, 400 West 15th Street, Austin, TX 78701 (8:00am–5:00pm, Mon–Fri)
what_to_send: Completed Form 2102 – Request for Universal Apostille
The original Texas-notarized document or certified copy of the public record
Payment ($15 per document)
A prepaid, pre-addressed return envelope or printed carrier label (no 'Bill Sender' or handwritten air bills)
tips: Certified records must have been issued within the past five years to be eligible.
You must name the destination country on Form 2102. Texas does not apostille documents for use within the U.S. or its territories.
Documents using the term 'Notario Publico' are rejected.
Online (RON) notarizations can be apostilled if submitted with the notary's ledger details and a proper online-notarization certificate.
Mailed requests are not pulled for walk-in service; they are processed in order of receipt.
sources: Texas SOS: Request a Universal Apostille
summary: Texas apostilles are issued by the Secretary of State's Authentications Unit for $15 per document. Mailed requests can take up to two weeks from receipt, while in-person service is same-day for up to 10 documents (walk-in Monday and Friday, appointment Tuesday to Thursday). Certified records must have been issued within the past five years.

name: Florida
authority: Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations (Apostille Section)
fee_note: $10.00 per document; or $20.00 per document for documents certified by any Florida county Clerk of the Court.
mail_time: Not published on the official page.
walkin_time: Not described on the official page; requests are mailed.
payment: Check or money order payable to the Florida Department of State, U.S. funds from a U.S. bank. No cash or credit cards.
addresses: Division of Corporations, 2415 N. Monroe Street, Suite 810, Tallahassee, FL 32303
what_to_send: The Apostille and Notarial Certificate Request Form
The original certified copy or original notarized document (no photocopies)
A self-addressed stamped envelope, or a prepaid air bill with your name as both sender and recipient
Payment
tips: Accepted Florida documents include birth and death certificates, circuit court documents, county clerk documents, marriage and divorce certificates, school transcripts and Florida-notarized documents (see the full list on the official page).
Federal documents go to the U.S. Department of State; other states' documents go to that state.
summary: Florida apostilles are issued by the Department of State, Division of Corporations, for $10 per document, or $20 for documents certified by a county Clerk of the Court. You mail the original with the request form and a return envelope. The official page does not publish a processing time.

name: Illinois
authority: Illinois Secretary of State, Index Department
fee_note: $2 for each apostille or certificate of authority; each document needs its own.
mail_time: 7 to 14 business days.
walkin_time: Available in Springfield, Chicago and select DMV+ locations; in most cases in-person requests are processed while you wait.
payment: One check or money order payable to the Illinois Secretary of State for the total fee.
addresses: Mail / Chicago office: Illinois Secretary of State, Index Department, 160 N. LaSalle Street, Suite 100, Chicago, IL 60601
Springfield office: 2701 S. Dirksen Parkway, Springfield, IL 62723
Select DMV+ locations: Chicago Flagship (125 W. Monroe), Aurora, Champaign, Lake Zurich, Melrose Park
what_to_send: Completed application from the official page
Original documents certified by a government official or notarized by an Illinois notary
Payment ($2 per document)
Self-addressed stamped return envelope
tips: Illinois cannot authenticate FBI background checks or federal documents. Those go to the U.S. Department of State.
summary: Illinois apostilles come from the Secretary of State's Index Department and cost $2 each. Mail requests take 7 to 14 business days, and walk-in service is available in Springfield, Chicago and select DMV+ locations. Illinois cannot apostille FBI background checks or other federal documents.

name: Pennsylvania
authority: Pennsylvania Department of State, Bureau of Notaries, Commissions and Legislation
fee_note: $15 per document (not per page).
mail_time: 5 to 7 business days after receipt (not including mailing time).
walkin_time: Processed while you wait; walk-ins 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Mon–Fri. The office asks you to arrive by 4 p.m., and notes the public entrance to the North Office Building closes at 3 p.m.
payment: Personal check, money order or cashier's check payable to 'Commonwealth of Pennsylvania' (U.S. institution, or U.S. dollars with routing number). No cash by mail.
addresses: North Office Building, 401 North Street, Room 201, Harrisburg, PA 17120
what_to_send: Original documents signed by the proper Pennsylvania official with their seal
A cover letter or the Request for Legalization of Documents form naming the destination country and your contact details
$15 per document
A self-addressed stamped envelope, or a prepaid UPS air bill (FedEx and DHL are not accepted for return)
tips: County documents signed by an assistant or deputy clerk are not accepted.
Marriage certificates must be signed by the register of wills or clerk of the orphans' court.
Death certificates must be signed by the state registrar, not a local registrar.
sources: PA DOS: Get Document Certifications & Apostilles
summary: Pennsylvania apostilles are issued by the Department of State's Bureau of Notaries, Commissions and Legislation for $15 per document. Mail requests take 5 to 7 business days after receipt, not counting mailing time. Walk-ins are processed while you wait, Monday to Friday.

name: North Carolina
authority: North Carolina Secretary of State, Authentications Division
fee_note: $10.00 per document. Duplicate originals: $10 each (adoption duplicates ordered at the same time: $5). The $10 fee may be refunded on request if a document is rejected and not processed.
mail_time: See the official 'Turn Around Times' page. Documented emergencies may qualify for expedited processing.
walkin_time: In-person delivery is accepted; see the official 'Getting Documents To and From Us' schedule.
payment: Check or money order payable to 'North Carolina Secretary of State'.
addresses: Address listed at the bottom of the official Authentications home page
what_to_send: Cover letter
Check or money order
Original document(s) with all certifications attached
A prepaid return envelope, or a courier label paid online with a bar code (see the official page for courier rules)
tips: Diplomas and transcripts from NC schools must be notarized by a North Carolina notary; a registrar's school seal alone is not acceptable.
Documents from NC Vital Records, Register of Deeds, Clerk of Superior Court and several state agencies do not need notarization.
North Carolina agency documents must be certified since April 1, 2000.
Non-English documents need a certified or notarized English translation.
sources: NC SOS: Process for Obtaining Authentication Certificates
summary: North Carolina apostilles are issued by the Secretary of State's Authentications Division for $10 per document. Diplomas and transcripts from North Carolina schools must be notarized by a North Carolina notary first. Current turnaround is posted on the office's official Turn Around Times page.

name: Georgia
authority: Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority (GSCCCA)
fee_note: $3.00 per apostille.
mail_time: Normally one to two business days.
walkin_time: Typically under twenty minutes; 9:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. Mon–Fri, no appointment.
payment: By mail: check or money order payable to GSCCCA, or credit card through the GSCCCA Credit Card Pre-Payment Voucher System. Walk-in: cash, check, money order or credit card.
addresses: GSCCCA, Attn: Notary Division, 1875 Century Blvd., Ste. 100, Atlanta, GA 30345
what_to_send: Original documents (certified copies of public records, or properly notarized Georgia documents)
A cover/request letter naming the destination country and your contact info
Payment
A prepaid self-addressed envelope or computer-generated FedEx/UPS air bill (no handwritten air bills)
tips: In Georgia, apostilles come from the GSCCCA, not the Secretary of State. The Secretary of State issues the 'Great Seal Certification' for non-Hague countries (404-656-2871).
For documents issued before 2000, the GSCCCA recommends getting a new certified copy.
summary: In Georgia, apostilles come from the GSCCCA (Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority), not the Secretary of State, and cost $3 each. Mail requests are normally processed in one to two business days, and walk-in requests typically take under twenty minutes.

name: New Jersey
authority: NJ Department of the Treasury, Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services (DORES)
fee_note: $25 per certificate (apostille); $5 per certificate when obtained in connection with the adoption of a child. A convenience fee may apply to online payment.
mail_time: Shown inside the state's online Apostille/Certification Service.
walkin_time: You can drop off documents with the confirmation page from the online service.
payment: Order and pay online (credit card or e-check) through the state's online Apostille/Certification Service, then mail or drop off the documents with the confirmation page.
addresses: The official page says to mail or drop off your documents, with the online order confirmation page, at the DORES Customer Service Center; it does not publish a separate apostille mailing address, so use the address given with your online order. (The Division's general address in the page footer is PO Box 628, Trenton, NJ 08625-0628.)
what_to_send: The original or certified copy bearing the original notarization or official certification
The confirmation page from the online Apostille/Certification Service
For notarized documents: the NJ notary's original inked signature and the signer's original inked signature
tips: Vital records from 1923 onward come from the NJ Department of Health; pre-1923 records from the NJ State Archives.
Attaching a notarized translation to a vital record means two apostilles and two fees.
New Jersey cannot apostille other states' vital records.
sources: NJ DORES: Apostilles and Notary Certifications
summary: New Jersey apostilles are handled by the Treasury's Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services (DORES) for $25 per certificate, or $5 in connection with an adoption. You start with the state's online Apostille/Certification Service, then send or drop off the documents with the confirmation page.

name: Arizona
authority: Arizona Secretary of State, Business Services Division
fee_note: $3 per document. In-person expedite fee: $25 (limit 6 documents). Documents going to Puerto Rico or a U.S. territory need an $18 notarial capacity certificate.
mail_time: 10–20 business days by mail.
walkin_time: In person (walk-in) with the $25 expedite fee, limit 6 documents. Effective November 2, 2026, Phoenix Business Services is by appointment only (book online); in-person service will no longer be at the 1700 W. Washington St. Executive Tower, and the appointment location is given when you book. Tucson office: 400 West Congress, Suite 221.
payment: Check or money order payable to "Arizona Secretary of State." Do not send cash by mail.
addresses: Filing by mail: Secretary of State, Attn: Apostille Dept., 1700 W. Washington Street, Fl. 7, Phoenix, AZ 85007-2808
Tucson office: 400 West Congress, Suite 221, Tucson, AZ 85701
what_to_send: Original notarized or certified document (no photocopies)
The Apostille request form from the official page
$3 per document
Return postage
tips: Arizona does not issue electronic apostilles.
Documents recorded by another state must go to that state.
Return labels (FedEx, UPS, DHL, etc.) must show your own mailing address as both sender and recipient.
summary: Arizona apostilles are issued by the Secretary of State's Business Services Division for $3 per document. Mail requests take 10 to 20 business days. In-person service adds a $25 expedite fee, and from November 2, 2026 in-person service in Phoenix is by appointment only.

name: Ohio
authority: Ohio Secretary of State, Client Service Center
fee_note: $5 per document for each apostille or authentication. The exact fee is required; do not send cash by mail.
mail_time: Documents are processed within two to three days of receipt, according to the office.
walkin_time: The request form says documents may be delivered in person to the Secretary of State's office if you need faster service. The office does not publish a separate same-day turnaround or apostille-specific walk-in hours; general office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern, Monday to Friday.
payment: Check, money order, or credit card. If you pay by card on a mailed request, include the office's Credit Card Authorization form (Form 100). Foreign checks or money orders are not accepted.
addresses: Mail or in person: Ohio Secretary of State, Client Service Center, 180 Civic Center Dr., Columbus, OH 43215-4138
what_to_send: A completed Authentication/Apostille Request Form (Form 8003)

The document(s): an original certified by an Ohio official, an Ohio birth or death certificate certified by the Ohio Department of Health, a certified copy from the probate court or county Clerk of Court, or a document properly notarized by an Ohio notary public
The exact fee of $5 per document by check, money order, or credit card authorization form (no cash)
A self-addressed stamped envelope or a prepaid express delivery label
tips: Documents notarized by a notary from another state or country, or certified by another state's official, will be rejected.
Ohio cannot apostille FBI background checks, documents issued under a federal seal or by a federal court, or citizenship documents unless issued by an Ohio county Clerk of Court.
Requests listing the United States as the destination country are rejected: apostilles cannot be used inside the U.S.
School records and transcripts must be notarized first; translations must be done, then notarized, before you submit them.
Never remove or reattach the apostille certificate; doing so invalidates it.
sources: Ohio SOS: Authentications and Apostilles FAQs
Ohio SOS: Authentication/Apostille Request Form (Form 8003, PDF)
summary: Ohio apostilles are issued by the Secretary of State's Client Service Center at 180 Civic Center Dr., Columbus, for $5 per document. Mailed requests are processed within two to three days of receipt, and you can deliver documents in person if you need faster service. Only documents issued by an Ohio official or notarized by an Ohio notary qualify.

name: Michigan
authority: Michigan Department of State, Office of the Great Seal
fee_note: $1 per document (per authentication, not per page), by check or money order payable to the State of Michigan. Do not send cash.
mail_time: The request form says to allow 4 to 6 weeks of processing after the office receives your request; the office's FAQ page gives a turnaround of 1 to 2 weeks. Expedited service is not available, and courier or priority mail is not processed any faster.
walkin_time: In-person service is by appointment only: at the Office of the Great Seal in Lansing on Mondays and Wednesdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., or at eight select Secretary of State offices. The office does not publish a same-day turnaround, and asks visitors to arrive at least one hour before closing.
payment: Check or money order payable to the State of Michigan for mailed requests (no cash). The office does not publish which payment methods are accepted at in-person appointments.
addresses: Mail: Michigan Department of State, Office of the Great Seal, 7064 Crowner Drive, Lansing, MI 48918
In person (appointment only): Office of the Great Seal, Richard H. Austin Building, 1st floor, 430 W. Allegan Street, Lansing, MI

Select Secretary of State offices (appointment only): Clinton Township (37015 Gratiot Ave.), Detroit (3046 W. Grand Blvd. L650, Cadillac Place), Flint (G-5512 Fenton Rd.), Grand Rapids (3665 28th Street SE, Centerpointe Mall 6-B), Lansing (3315 E. Michigan Ave.), Livonia (17176 Farmington Rd.), Marquette (2025 Highway 41 West, Marquette Mall), Pontiac (1270 Pontiac Rd.)
what_to_send: A completed and signed Authentication Request Form, which names the destination country (not the USA; for China, mark Mainland, Hong Kong or Macao)
The document(s), signed by an authorized Michigan official or a commissioned Michigan notary, with original signatures
$1 per document by check or money order payable to the State of Michigan (no cash)
A self-addressed stamped envelope or a prepaid air bill (FedEx, UPS or USPS) listing yourself as both sender and receiver; the office does not pay return postage
An English translation of any document in a foreign language
tips: Vital records (birth, marriage, divorce, death) must be certified copies from the Michigan State Registrar, a Michigan county clerk, or a city clerk in Wayne, Macomb or Oakland County.
Documents from a court clerk, a register of deeds or another state must be notarized before the Office of the Great Seal can authenticate them.

Stamped, photocopied or facsimile signatures are rejected, and the notary block must show the notary's full name, signature, date, commission expiration date and county of commission (plus county of execution if different).
Michigan notaries cannot certify that a copy is a true copy; the issuer, or the person named on the document, makes the true copy statement and the notary acknowledges that signature.
Apostilles are only for Hague Convention countries; other countries get a Certificate of Authority, which has the same requirements and the same $1 fee.
sources: Michigan SOS: Document authentication and apostille
Michigan SOS: Document authentication FAQs (Office of the Great Seal)
Michigan SOS: Authentication Request Form (PDF, Rev. 8/23)
Michigan SOS: Office of the Great Seal
summary: Michigan apostilles are issued by the Department of State's Office of the Great Seal for $1 per document, by mail to 7064 Crowner Drive, Lansing, or in person by appointment in Lansing or at eight select Secretary of State offices. The request form says to allow 4 to 6 weeks after receipt, and expedited service is not available.

name: Washington
authority: Washington Secretary of State, Corporations & Charities Division (Apostilles Program)
fee_note: $15 per document (a document can be more than one page), by check or money order in U.S. dollars payable to the Secretary of State. Expedited processing adds $100 per 10 documents; same-day in-person service adds $150 for the first 10 documents.
mail_time: The office says standard processing is typically 7 to 10 business days after it receives your order, and longer when volumes are high. Expedited processing (extra $100 per 10 documents) is typically 2 to 3 business days. Documents come back by regular first-class mail unless you include a prepaid traceable return label or envelope.
walkin_time: Same-day in-person service is offered in Tumwater (Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Friday 8 a.m. to 3 p.m.) and in Cheney (Monday to Wednesday and Friday 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.; closed Thursdays). Documents must arrive 30 minutes before closing, and same-day service can be limited by cutoff times and volume. The fee is $15 per document plus $150 for the first 10 documents ($100 more for each additional 10).
payment: Check or money order in U.S. dollars payable to the Secretary of State for mailed requests. The office does not publish on the apostille pages which payment methods it takes for in-person same-day service.
addresses: Mail (Corporations & Charities Division, USPS): PO Box 40234, Olympia, WA 98504-0234 (the apostille request form PDF lists PO Box 40228 with the same ZIP+4; the contact page says the division has only one mailing address, PO Box 40234, so check with the office before mailing)
In person, same-day (Western Washington): 243 Israel Rd SE, Tumwater, WA 98501 (this address accepts overnight deliveries by commercial carrier only)
In person, same-day (Eastern Washington): 960 Washington St, Cheney, WA 99004 (cannot receive mail)
phone: 360-725-0377 (option 3 for apostilles on the request form); the office lists an apostille email on its contact page
what_to_send: A completed Apostille Authentication Request Form, which names the country that requested the document, with your name, address, email and phone number

The original (unaltered) or certified copy of a document issued by a Washington government entity, a certified Washington court document, or a personal document notarized by a Washington notary with a complete notarial certificate
$15 per document by check or money order payable to the Secretary of State (add $100 per 10 documents to expedite)
Optional: a prepaid traceable return label or envelope, which the office says to use if the order is time sensitive or going outside the United States
tips: Washington issues one universal certificate that works as an apostille for Hague Convention countries or as a certificate of authentication for other countries; documents for non-member countries may need further certification from the U.S. Department of State, the embassy, or both.
Vital records (birth, death, marriage, divorce, letter of single status) must be apostilled by the state that issued them, and only on an original or certified copy.

The office does not authenticate federal documents. FBI background checks go to the U.S. Department of State; a Washington State Patrol background check needs a notarized clearance letter from the State Patrol (include the original fingerprint card if the check was fingerprint-based).

Notary certificates must be complete, show a Washington notary's stamp and signature with matching names, the commission expiration date, the date, the act performed (in English) and the Washington county, and must not be stapled to the document.

Washington college and university transcripts must be official and signed by the registrar and do not need notarizing; out-of-state school documents, including transcripts and diplomas, are accepted only as copies notarized by a Washington notary (the page says it can process official transcripts only from Washington schools, with diplomas the exception).

Business records (certificates or certified copies from the Corporations Division) must be ordered at the same time as the apostille using the Business Records Request Form; they cannot be ordered online for this purpose.
sources: WA SOS: Apostille Frequently Asked Questions
WA SOS: Apostille Authentication Request Form (PDF, rev. 6/2025)
WA SOS: Contact Us (addresses, hours, in-person services)
summary: Washington apostilles are issued by the Secretary of State's Corporations & Charities Division for $15 per document, by mail or in person the same day in Tumwater or Cheney (extra $150 same-day fee). The office says standard processing typically takes 7 to 10 business days and expedited processing 2 to 3 business days (extra $100 per 10 documents).

name: Virginia
authority: Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth, Authentication Division
fee_note: $10 per document (not per page), payable to the Secretary of the Commonwealth. If several documents were signed by the same official (notary, deputy clerk, etc.) on the same date for the same country, it is $10 for the first and $5 for each additional one. Overpayments of $5 or less may not be refunded.
mail_time: The office says the general turnaround for mailed packages is 7 to 10 business days from when you send them, and it can only check status after that. A notice on its main authentications page (seen 2026-11-15) says that, because of the holiday season and very high mail volume, processing and return shipping currently take approximately 4 weeks. Documents left in the drop box at 400 East Cary Street are processed and returned by mail within 5 to 7 business days.
walkin_time: In person is by appointment only, Monday to Thursday, at 400 East Cary Street, Richmond; without an appointment you will not be seen. Appointments are booked online only on Fridays at 10:00 a.m. for the following week, with up to 10 documents per customer or family. The office says it can process most authentications the same day as the appointment if documents are properly notarized or issued.
payment: Check or money order payable to the Secretary of the Commonwealth. The office does not publish whether cards are accepted at appointments.
addresses: USPS mail: Secretary of the Commonwealth, Authentication Division, 1111 East Broad Street, Richmond, VA 23219
FedEx, UPS and DHL: Secretary of the Commonwealth, Authentication Division, 400 East Cary Street, Richmond, VA 23219
In person (appointment only) and drop box: 400 East Cary Street, Richmond, VA 23219 (behind the Virginia Department of Health)
what_to_send: A cover letter created through the office's online authentications portal (register or log in to make it)
The document(s), each held together with a staple or paperclip, with original signatures
The fee: $10 per document ($5 for each additional document signed by the same official on the same date for the same country), by check or money order payable to the Secretary of the Commonwealth
A self-addressed, prepaid return mailer (UPS, FedEx, USPS, etc.); for FedEx, UPS or DHL, list your own name and address as both sender and recipient
tips: Notarized documents must be notarized by a Virginia notary within the past 12 months, with the county or city, date, notarial statement, notary signature, commission expiration date, registration number and a seal matching the notary's commissioned name exactly. The notarization must be in English.

Vital records (birth, death, marriage, divorce) cannot be notarized and must be issued by the Virginia Department of Health Vital Records or a local DMV within the past 12 months; circuit court marriage certificates and court records need the Certification of Official Record (triple seal), also within 12 months.

Virginia will not authenticate documents notarized in another state, out-of-state vital records, out-of-state diplomas or transcripts, or electronic (eNotary) notarizations. FBI checks and other federal documents go to the U.S. Department of State.

If you list the office as the sender on a FedEx, UPS or DHL return label, your documents come back by regular mail without tracking; packages sent with no return envelope or postage also come back by regular USPS mail without tracking.

The office does not require translations, does not notarize, and is not affiliated with any apostille company. Virginia staples the apostille to the document, which the Hague Special Commission accepts.
sources: Virginia Secretary of the Commonwealth: Authentications
Virginia Secretary of the Commonwealth: How to Submit (fees, appointments, mail)
Virginia Secretary of the Commonwealth: Types of Documents
Virginia Secretary of the Commonwealth: Why Would a Document Be Rejected?
summary: Virginia apostilles come from the Secretary of the Commonwealth's Authentication Division in Richmond for $10 per document ($5 for each additional document signed by the same official on the same date for the same country). Mail them in or book a Monday-to-Thursday appointment, where most are done the same day; mail usually takes 7 to 10 business days, but the office currently warns of about 4 weeks for the holiday season.

name: Massachusetts
authority: Secretary of the Commonwealth, Public Records Division, Commissions Section
fee_note: $6 per document for an apostille or certification, by check or money order payable to the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Cash is not recommended because the office cannot refund cash lost in transit.
mail_time: The office says mailed requests are processed within two to three weeks. It does not publish a separate return-shipping time.
walkin_time: At the Boston counter (One Ashburton Place, Room 1719) up to three documents per customer are done at the counter; four or more documents can be picked up after 3 p.m. on the next business day, and anything dropped off after 4 p.m. is picked up the next business day, with no exceptions. Requests can also be brought to the Springfield and Fall River offices, where the office says the number of documents and turnaround times vary. Office hours are not published on the apostille page.
payment: Check or money order only, payable to the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Credit cards are not accepted as pre-payment for express mail return services.
addresses: Boston (mail or in person): Secretary of the Commonwealth, Commissions Section, One Ashburton Place, Room 1719, Boston, MA 02108
Springfield (mail or in person): Secretary of the Commonwealth, 436 Dwight Street, Room 102, Springfield, MA 01103

what_to_send: The completed Apostille/Certification Request Form

The original document(s), signed by a Massachusetts notary public, justice of the peace, city or town clerk (or assistant), court clerk (or assistant) or Registrar of Vital Records; photocopied signatures can't be certified
The country of destination for the documents
The fee: $6 per document, by check or money order payable to the Commonwealth of Massachusetts
A prepaid return envelope (first-class mail needs a self-addressed stamped envelope; FedEx, DHL or other express return needs a prepaid envelope with a billing account number)
tips: Massachusetts does not authenticate federal or out-of-state documents, and does not authenticate notarized copies of government-issued documents (for example a notarized photocopy of an FBI background check or of another state's certificate of good standing). FBI checks go to the U.S. Department of State.

For a Massachusetts school transcript or diploma, have the school registrar certify the record in front of a notary, who notarizes the registrar's signature; then send it for the apostille. Out-of-state school records must be certified by their own state.
Before you go, check that the notary signed exactly as commissioned, completed the notarial certificate, wrote the commission expiration date clearly, and applied a legible seal.

Certified copies of marriage certificates come from the city or town clerk where the license was filed; divorce decrees from the court clerk where the decree was filed; birth certificates from the Office of Vital Records (617-740-2600) or the local city or town clerk.
Missing information (such as the destination country) can delay the certification. If nothing is checked for the return method on the form, the order is held at the office for pickup.

name: Colorado
authority: Colorado Secretary of State, Authentications Program
fee_note: $5 per apostille or authentication for mail-in or drop-off (routine) service; $15 per apostille for expedited service, which is walk-in only. No credit or debit cards.
mail_time: The office does not publish a processing time. It says it is experiencing longer than normal wait times, that mailed documents are worked in the order received and sent back as soon as possible, and that its mail goes through a state distribution center before reaching USPS. Documents are not processed on weekends or holidays.
walkin_time: Expedited service ($15 per apostille) is for documents hand delivered to the Denver office before 4:30 PM. The office tries to process them while you wait and says expedited service can generally be completed in under an hour, but with heavy demand it may take longer and you may be asked to come back. Routine drop-off ($5) is also available; the office emails or phones you when documents are ready for pickup. Office hours are not published on the apostille page.
payment: The request form says cash, check or money order are accepted (no credit or debit cards), but the office's general information page says expedited service must be paid by check or money order, so bring a check or money order to be safe. Make checks and money orders payable to "Colorado Secretary of State". Do not send cash through the mail. A CO SOS prepaid account can also be listed on the form.
addresses: Mail or in person: Colorado Secretary of State, Authentications Program, 1700 Broadway, Ste. 550, Denver, CO 80290
what_to_send: The original document, with a Colorado notary public signature, or certified by Colorado Vital Records or by a Colorado County Clerk's office
The completed Apostilles & Authentications Request Form (NAUTH), listing the foreign country where the documents will be presented and the number of apostilles
Payment: $5 per apostille by check or money order payable to "Colorado Secretary of State" (no cash by mail)
Your return choice: hold for pickup, standard USPS return (free), or a prepaid FedEx or UPS label
tips: Colorado will not issue apostilles or authentications for documents used in the United States or its territories (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands).

The office does not notarize documents and offers no online apostilles. It does offer a free pre-check: email a PDF of your document to Authentications@coloradosos.gov and staff will review it and give feedback before you submit.

To avoid delays, signatures must be original (not stamped or photocopied), every blank must be filled in or crossed out, and the notary statement must be complete (state, county and date) and in English, even if the document is in another language.

Out-of-state government documents (birth, death or marriage certificates) can't be authenticated by Colorado, except as a certified copy made by a Colorado notary. Certificates of Naturalization: get a certified true copy from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and send it to the U.S. Department of State.
If you include a prepaid FedEx or UPS label, don't put the Secretary of State's name or address as the return address, or the documents will be returned by standard mail.

Colorado birth and death certificates come from the Vital Records Office; marriage licenses, divorce decrees and other court documents come from the County Clerk and Recorder or Clerk of the District Court where they were issued.

name: Maryland
authority: Maryland Secretary of State, Certification Desk
fee_note: $5 per document for an apostille or certification. By mail, pay by U.S. check or U.S. money order made out to the Secretary of State (one payment per order); in person you can also pay by credit or debit card.
mail_time: The office publishes processing times by how you send it: regular mail is 7 to 14 business days; USPS Priority Mail is a maximum of 3-4 days; FedEx and UPS are around a 3-4 day turnaround. The Certification Desk is closed on Maryland state holidays.
walkin_time: The official page currently says walk-in service is not available at this time and in-person service is by scheduled appointment (booked online from the page), with a limit of 10 documents per customer per day and space for no more than 2 family members. It warns that appointments may change because of building construction, and that once construction begins the office will move to mail-in only. Certification hours are 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Monday through Friday. The page does not say whether in-person documents are done while you wait; call 410-974-5521 before going.
payment: By mail: U.S. check or U.S. money order made out to the Secretary of State, one payment per order (don't staple the check). In person: check, money order, or credit or debit card.
addresses: Mail: Certification Desk, Office of the Secretary of State, 16 Francis Street, 1st floor, Annapolis, MD 21401
In person (by appointment): Office of the Secretary of State, Wineland Building, 16 Francis Street, Annapolis, MD 21401
phone: 410-974-5521 (Certification Desk); 410-260-3852 and email dlCertifications_sos@maryland.gov (certification of documents to be used outside the U.S.)
what_to_send: The original document: a Maryland state or county issued document (for example a birth or death certificate, marriage certificate, divorce decree or criminal records status certification) with the seal and signature of the issuing department, or a notarized document already certified by the Clerk of the Circuit Court
The completed Mailing Checklist for Documents to be Certified for International Use, including the country where the documents will be used and a daytime phone number and email
Payment: $5 per document by U.S. check or U.S. money order made out to the Secretary of State (one payment per order; do not staple the check)
A postage-paid self-addressed return envelope, or a prepaid FedEx, UPS or other express envelope (keep your tracking numbers)
tips: Notarized documents need an extra step first: take the document to the Clerk of the Circuit Court in the county where the notary was commissioned (the county is on the notary's seal) to certify the notary, then send it to the Secretary of State. If a former Circuit Court clerk signed that certification, call 410-974-5521 to confirm it can be accepted.

School records (transcripts, grades, diplomas): get them from the school, have a notary open the sealed envelope and notarize the record, have the Circuit Court clerk in the notary's county certify the notary, then send it to the Secretary of State.

Federal documents such as FBI background checks, USCIS documents and born-abroad birth certificates go to the U.S. Department of State, not Maryland. Naturalization and immigration documents can't be notarized, whether originals or copies.

For a Hague Convention country you get an apostille and you're done. For a non-Hague country, Maryland issues a standard certification, which must then go to the U.S. Department of State before the destination country's embassy.

If you don't have a current copy of a state or county document, call 410-974-5521 to confirm the office can authenticate it. The office says it cannot guarantee that a foreign country will accept the document.

By mail, the office says regular mail takes 7 to 14 business days and USPS Priority, FedEx or UPS about 3-4 days; walk-in service is currently not available, so in-person visits are by appointment (9 a.m. to 1 p.m. weekdays, up to 10 documents).

name: Minnesota
authority: Minnesota Secretary of State, Business Services (Apostille Authentication)
fee_note: $5 per apostille certificate, issued per document (the office's example: a Minnesota birth certificate plus a three-page notarized transcript = two documents = $10). By mail, pay by check or money order made out to MN Secretary of State; at an in-person appointment you can also pay by credit card, debit card or cash.
mail_time: The office does not publish a processing time. Its FAQ says documents are processed in the order they are received; sending your request overnight with a prepaid overnight return label speeds up delivery but does not speed up processing. For urgent requests when appointments are booked out, the office asks you to email apostille.oss@state.mn.us.
walkin_time: No walk-ins: in-person service is by appointment only, booked online (sos.mn.gov/appointment) or by calling 651-296-2803, option 2. Appointments open fourteen days in advance and take up to 10 documents. The office does not say whether documents are finished while you wait, and it does not publish counter hours on its apostille page.
payment: By mail: check or money order made out to MN Secretary of State (the request form also lists cashier's check, cash at your own risk, or charging a Secretary of State client account; no credit card or wire transfer by mail; U.S. dollars only). In person: credit card, debit card, cash, check or money order.
addresses: Mail: Minnesota Secretary of State, First National Bank Building, 332 Minnesota Street, Suite N201, Saint Paul, MN 55101
In person (by appointment): same address, First National Bank Building, 332 Minnesota Street, Suite N201, Saint Paul, MN 55101
what_to_send: The original document: a Minnesota certified copy (for example a birth or death certificate from the Minnesota Department of Health, a marriage certificate, divorce decree or judgment certified by the county) or a document properly notarized by a Minnesota Notary Public. Photocopies of certified records are not accepted.
The completed Apostille/Authentication Request Form, with the number of documents and how you want them returned (pick up, your prepaid return envelope, or regular U.S. mail)
Payment: $5 per document by check or money order made out to MN Secretary of State
Optional: a prepaid FedEx, USPS Priority Mail or UPS label if you want tracking; otherwise the office returns documents by regular U.S. mail at no charge and without tracking
tips: Minnesota issues only one certificate, an apostille, for every foreign country, Hague member or not (since May 15, 2018). If the destination country does not accept an apostille, the office says to contact that country's embassy or consulate for your options.

Transcripts and diplomas from Minnesota schools, colleges and universities must be notarized by a Minnesota Notary Public; a school official's signature and seal alone is not accepted. If a school gives you a sealed envelope, the Secretary of State must open it to see the notarization.

The notarization must be in English and include all six elements of Minn. Stat. 358.65: jurisdiction, notarial statement, the title Notary Public, date, wet-ink signature and notary stamp. The notary's name and expiration date on the stamp must match the commission. The office does not notarize documents.
Remote or electronic notarization is not accepted: a printed document signed electronically by a Minnesota notary is treated as a copy and must be notarized again before an apostille can be issued.

FBI background checks go to the U.S. Department of State, not Minnesota. For a Minnesota state background check, get a notarized letter from the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension. Birth, death or school records from another state must be apostilled by that state.

Driver's licenses and passports: send a photocopy notarized as a true and correct copy by a Minnesota notary, never the original. A translation is apostilled separately from the certified record it translates, so it counts as a second document.

Conflicts between official pages: the apostille page lists check or money order for mail, while the request form it links to also allows cash (not recommended) or a client account. For more than 10 documents, the FAQ says to mail or drop them off with payment, while the appointment page says to contact the office for special arrangements. Ask apostille.oss@state.mn.us if either matters for you.
You can verify an apostille Minnesota issued on or after May 15, 2018 at apostille.sos.state.mn.us using its file number and date.

summary: Minnesota apostilles come from the Secretary of State at 332 Minnesota Street, Suite N201, Saint Paul, for $5 per document, by mail or by in-person appointment (no walk-ins). The office does not publish a processing time; it says requests are processed in the order received.

name: Tennessee
authority: Tennessee Secretary of State, Business Services Division (Office of Authentications, ATS Section)
fee_note: $2 per apostille or authentication, charged per document (request form SS-4504: number requested x $2.00). Fees must be sent with the request. The Secretary of State's apostille guide and request form do not list accepted payment methods; the Tennessee Office of Vital Records says to pay the apostille fee by check made payable to the Tennessee Secretary of State.
mail_time: The office does not publish a processing time for mailed requests. Documents sent without a proper prepaid express label are processed and returned by regular mail.
walkin_time: Walk-in service at the customer service desk, 312 Rosa L. Parks Ave, 3rd Floor, Nashville, Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Central (closed state holidays). Arrive by 2:00 p.m. to receive same-day service. No appointment is mentioned.
payment: Not listed on the Secretary of State's apostille guide or request form. The Tennessee Office of Vital Records says to pay the $2 apostille fee by check made payable to the Tennessee Secretary of State. Ask the Apostilles & Authentications Section (615-741-0536, TNSOS.ATS@tnsos.gov) before paying another way, especially in person.
addresses: Mail: Office of Authentications, Tennessee Secretary of State, Business Services Division, ATTN: ATS Section, 312 Rosa L. Parks Ave, 6th Floor, Nashville, TN 37243
In person: customer service desk, 312 Rosa L. Parks Ave, 3rd Floor, Nashville, TN 37243
what_to_send: The original Tennessee public document: a vital record signed by the State Registrar (birth, death, marriage or divorce certificate) or a Secretary of State document needs no notarization; state and county records must have been certified within the past two years.

For notarized documents (school transcripts, diplomas, powers of attorney, affidavits): first have it notarized by a Tennessee notary, then have the notary's signature certified by the County Clerk of the county where the notary was commissioned. Tell the office the county of certification.
The completed Apostille or Authentication Request Form (SS-4504), naming the country where the document will be used (apostille for Hague countries, authentication for others)
Payment of $2 per document

Optional: a prepaid FedEx/UPS return label with your own name as both sender and recipient for express return; for an international return address a prepaid USPS International, DHL Express, FedEx International or UPS Worldwide label is required, plus any customs paperwork
tips: Tennessee adds a County Clerk step: a notarized document is not accepted until the County Clerk of the county where the notary was commissioned has certified the notary's signature.

Return labels must show your name as both the sender and the recipient; the office cannot use a label naming the Tennessee Secretary of State as sender. Documents going to an international address without the proper prepaid label are rejected.

Accepted (per the office's list): Tennessee vital records, state court records, TBI background checks, county records certified within two years, Tennessee school transcripts and diplomas (registrar or president signature notarized and county-certified), Tennessee motor vehicle records, and Tennessee notarized documents. A photocopy of a diploma, driver license or U.S. passport must be attached to an affidavit by the person it was issued to, notarized and county-certified; passport copies get an authentication only.

Not accepted: out-of-state documents, federal documents (except U.S. passport copies as above), foreign documents, documents to be used inside the U.S., and non-English documents unless a notarized, county-certified translator's statement and English translation are attached. FBI background checks go to the U.S. Department of State.

If you need a certified copy of a Tennessee vital record too, the Office of Vital Records will forward it to the Secretary of State for the apostille if you include a separate check for $2 per document made payable to the Tennessee Secretary of State.
An authentication (non-Hague country) must then be certified by the U.S. Department of State Office of Authentications; an apostille needs no further U.S. step.

Hours conflict between official pages: the apostille guide gives in-person apostille hours as 8:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Central, while the Business Services contact page lists division hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Either way, arrive by 2:00 p.m. for same-day service.
You can verify a Tennessee apostille or authentication with the Secretary of State's online verification tool (tncab.tnsos.gov/portal/apostille-search).

Arrive at the 3rd-floor counter by 2:00 p.m. Central for same-day service; the office does not publish a processing time for mail.

name: Indiana
authority: Indiana Secretary of State, Business Services Division (Authentications)
fee_note: $2.00 per apostille authentication (nonrefundable). No fee for birth and death certificates, adoption documents, and student transcripts and diplomas; the request form (State Form 56720) also exempts documents prepared by the Secretary of State and words the first item as Indiana birth and death certificates.
mail_time: Mailed requests are processed daily; the office's FAQ says processing normally takes 1–2 business days from the date of receipt, plus return shipping. The office cannot provide expedited shipping, so include a prepaid expedited return label if the documents are time-sensitive.
walkin_time: Walk-ins are accepted at 302 W. Washington Street, Room E-018, Indianapolis, Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.: without an appointment the office processes up to 5 documents while you wait; with an appointment (priority service, booked online) up to 10. Larger requests need a self-addressed, stamped envelope: documents received by noon are mailed the next business day, after noon within two business days.
payment: Mail: check or money order payable to "Secretary of State". In person: credit card, debit card, check or money order, paid on arrival.
addresses: Mail: Indiana Secretary of State, Authentications, 302 W. Washington Street, Room E-018, Indianapolis, IN 46204
In person: same address, Room E-018 (the office says it has no branch offices)
what_to_send: The original or a certified copy of the Indiana document. Birth, death, marriage and divorce certificates do not need notarization; any other document must be properly notarized, with a completed notarial certificate (notary's signature, seal, jurisdiction, date and signer's name).
The completed Request for Apostille Authentication (State Form 56720), naming the destination country
The fee: $2.00 per document unless exempt (birth and death certificates, adoption documents, student transcripts and diplomas)
A self-addressed, stamped return envelope (a prepaid return envelope is required for any international return); for overnight return include a pre-addressed, prepaid airbill
tips: Indiana charges no fee to apostille birth and death certificates, adoption documents, or student transcripts and diplomas, so many personal-document requests cost nothing beyond postage.

Indiana married couples: the marriage license must first be certified by the current circuit court clerk of the county where the marriage occurred. A divorce decree must be a copy of the final decree from the county where it was entered.

School transcripts and diplomas: the school's registrar or principal signs a statement certifying the record in front of a notary, who notarizes it; the office publishes a short-form example and advises checking the destination country's preferred method first.
Translations are not done by the office; a translation must be notarized before the office can process it.

Since July 1, 2022 Indiana issues one trilingual certificate format (Model Apostille Single Certificate) for all requests, stapled to the front of the signed page with a blue-ink state seal and a unique verification number. Do not remove the certificate: that invalidates it.

Not accepted: out-of-state documents (contact the issuing state), federal documents such as FBI background checks, citizenship documents and federal court documents (these go to the U.S. Department of State), and documents for use in the United States or Puerto Rico.

Mail return rules differ slightly between official pages: the web page says a self-addressed stamped envelope must be provided, while the request form says that without an envelope or label documents are returned by regular mail to the U.S. address on the form. Include the envelope to be safe.

Fee-exemption wording also differs: the web page lists birth and death certificates, adoption documents and transcripts/diplomas; the request form says Indiana birth and death certificates and adds documents prepared by the Secretary of State.

Mail requests normally take 1–2 business days from receipt, and walk-ins get up to 5 documents done while they wait (10 with an appointment).

name: Missouri
authority: Missouri Secretary of State, Business Services: Notaries & Commissions Unit
fee_note: $10 per certification or authentication (apostille). The office's examples: one document with several notarizations by the same notary is $10; several documents notarized by the same notary are $10 per document; one document with notarizations by different notaries is $10 per notary. State law caps the fee for certain adoption documents at $100 per child per adoption (or per group of children adopted at the same time). Credit card payments add a convenience fee of 2% + $0.25, paid to the e-payment vendor.
mail_time: The office's Notary Handbook says documents received in the mail are given same-day or next-day service, plus mail time both ways. Documents come back by regular mail unless you include a prepaid envelope with an addressed air bill.
walkin_time: Walk-in customers can receive same-day processing at 600 W. Main St., Room 322, Jefferson City (Notary Handbook: walk-in hours 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; contact page: 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday except legal holidays). The handbook says branch offices in St. Louis, Kansas City and Springfield can also provide this service.
payment: Check or money order payable to the "Secretary of State's Office", or MasterCard, Visa, American Express or Discover (by mail, include the completed credit card payment sheet; card payments add a 2% + $0.25 convenience fee).
addresses: Mail (apostille page and cover letter): Commissions, Secretary of State's Office, 600 West Main, Room 322, Jefferson City, MO 65101

Regular mail (contact page and Notary Handbook): Notaries & Commissions Unit, James C. Kirkpatrick State Information Center, PO Box 784, Jefferson City, MO 65102; use the 600 West Main, Room 322 street address for express deliveries
In person: James C. Kirkpatrick State Information Center, 600 West Main, Room 322, Jefferson City, MO 65101

Branch offices: 815 Olive Street, Suite 150, St. Louis, MO 63101 (314-340-7490); Kansas City State Office Building, 615 E. 13th St., Fifth Floor, Suite 513, Kansas City, MO 64106 (816-889-2925); Springfield State Office Building, 149 Park Central Sq., Suite 624, Springfield, MO 65806 (417-895-6330)
what_to_send: The Missouri document, prepared as the office requires: birth certificate as a certified copy from the Bureau of Vital Records; marriage license as a certified copy from the Recorder of Deeds of the county of the marriage (or a statement related to marriage from Vital Records); divorce decree as a certified copy from the Circuit Clerk of the county where it is recorded; school documents as a certified copy from the school; notarized documents with the full notarization (notarial paragraph, notary's signature and seal)
The completed Apostille/Authentication Cover Letter, with the number of documents and the country of use
Payment: $10 per apostille/authentication by check or money order payable to the Secretary of State's Office, or the completed credit card payment sheet
A prepaid return envelope with an addressed air bill if you don't want regular-mail return (required for special delivery when paying by card)
tips: Mail or drive? The Notary Handbook says mailed documents get same-day or next-day service and walk-ins can get same-day processing, so the main difference is mail transit time both ways. If you go to a branch office (St. Louis, Kansas City, Springfield), call it first: the handbook lists branches for this service, but the apostille web page only gives the Jefferson City address.

Missouri birth certificates ordered through VitalChek can be forwarded straight to the Secretary of State: choose the "Apostille/Authentication" reason when ordering. Vital Records says certificates go to the Secretary of State about once a week, and the Secretary of State then contacts you for details and payment.

School documents: the registrar or other school authority signs a statement on the back of the diploma or transcript saying it is the original (or a copy of the original) and the date issued, in front of a notary who notarizes it. Don't alter the face of the diploma.

Missouri notaries cannot certify copies of birth or death certificates, divorce decrees or marriage licenses, and cannot certify documents from other states or countries; get certified copies from the issuing agency.

The office can forward finished documents directly to a third party (such as a consulate) if you enclose a stamped envelope addressed to them, and returns by overnight mail if you enclose a prepaid self-addressed mailer.
The destination country decides the certificate: an apostille for Hague Convention countries, an authentication for others.

Official pages differ on a few details: the contact page lists hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., while the Notary Handbook gives walk-in hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; the apostille page and cover letter say checks are payable to the Secretary of State's Office, while the handbook says Director of Revenue; and the apostille page says to mail documents to 600 West Main, Room 322, while the contact page and handbook give PO Box 784 for regular mail. Follow the apostille page and cover letter, or call 573-751-2783 to confirm.

name: Wisconsin
authority: Wisconsin Secretary of State, Certification Desk (apostilles and authentications); the Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions (DFI) also issues apostilles
fee_note: Secretary of State: $10 per document for standard service, or $35 per document for expedited service (the FAQ describes this as an additional $25 expedited fee). Fees are per certificate issued, and a document can have multiple pages. DFI charges the same: $10 per document standard, $35 per document expedited.
mail_time: Secretary of State standard service is estimated at 7-20 days from the day the office receives your documents (how-to page; the FAQ says 7-20 business days and the February 2026 order form says 7-10+ business days); expedited is 2-4 business days (how-to page) or 1-3 business days (FAQ and order form). Times are estimates and don't include shipping. DFI, which issues apostilles only, lists 3-7 business days standard and 1-2 business days expedited, not including mail time.
walkin_time: Walk-in expedited service is generally available same-day at the Secretary of State's office, Room B41W in the basement of the Wisconsin State Capitol, Madison. Office hours: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.
payment: Checks and money orders payable to "Wisconsin Secretary of State" (no starter checks, per the order form), or cash. The how-to page also lists card, and the instruction sheet lists Apple Pay and credit cards except American Express, but the FAQ and order form list only cash, check or money order. The office can't make change for bills larger than $50. Orders started in the online portal are paid online. DFI takes payment only through its online portal (credit card, debit card or e-check).
addresses: USPS mail: Secretary of State, Certification Desk, P.O. Box 7848, Madison, WI 53707-7848
FedEx or UPS courier: Secretary of State, Certification Desk, State Capitol Mailroom, 17 W. Main Street, Madison, WI 53703-3960
In person / drop-off: Wisconsin State Capitol, Room B41W (basement level), Madison, WI 53703

DFI (apostilles only, order online first): Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions, PO Box 7838, Madison, WI 53707-7838; physical address Division of Corporate and Consumer Services, 4822 Madison Yards Way, North Tower, Madison, WI 53705
phone: Secretary of State: (608) 266-8888 (ext. 5 on the denied-request checklist); Apostilles@wisconsin.gov. DFI: (608) 266-8915; DFIApostille@dfi.wisconsin.gov
what_to_send: The Authentication & Apostille Order Form (one per destination country, and one per service speed if you split an order), naming the country that will receive the document; the office doesn't issue certificates for use in the United States or its territories

One original document for each certificate requested: a certified copy from the Wisconsin official who issued it (for example, a vital record from a Register of Deeds or the State Registrar), or a document fully notarized by a Wisconsin notary with wet-ink signature and a stamped or embossed seal
Payment: $10 per document standard or $35 per document expedited
A prepaid return USPS envelope or a self-addressed prepaid FedEx or UPS label, or tick in-person pickup in Room B41W (no DHL or FedEx Ground)
tips: Where is my document? The Secretary of State processes documents in the order received, with expedited orders first. Its FAQ asks you not to request a status update until more than 7 days after it received an expedited order, or more than 30 days for standard; email Apostilles@wisconsin.gov with the last name on the order form, the destination country, the date sent or received, and how you submitted it (drop off, USPS, FedEx, UPS).

Wisconsin has two competent authorities: the Secretary of State and the Department of Financial Institutions. Both issue apostilles for Hague Convention countries; only the Secretary of State issues authentications for non-Hague countries. DFI orders start in its online portal (free account), and DFI also offers e-Apostilles, but not for vital records.

Notarized documents: the Secretary of State accepts only wet-ink, stamped or embossed notarizations by a Wisconsin notary and cannot accept digital or electronic notarizations. Each notarization must show the venue (State of Wisconsin, county), an approved notarial statement, the date, and the notary's signature, seal and commission expiration date.

Vital records: don't alter or copy them; photocopies or notarized copies of vital records can't be processed. Hospital-created birth certificates and church-signed marriage certificates are refused; get a certified copy from the Register of Deeds or the State Registrar at the Vital Records Office.

School documents not issued by the University of Wisconsin (including high school and private college records) must first be certified by the school's registrar or another authorized official, with signature and title, and that signature notarized by a Wisconsin notary. The office won't process documents from schools outside Wisconsin.
The office cannot process federal documents (including FBI background checks), federal court documents, or vital records and other documents issued by another state or country.

You can start a Secretary of State order and pay in its online order portal (MyWisconsinID login required), but you still mail or deliver the documents; online orders are subject to cancellation if documents aren't received within 60 days.

Official pages differ on a few details: standard processing is 7-20 days (how-to page), 7-20 business days (FAQ) or 7-10+ business days (order form, rev. 2/2026); expedited is 2-4 business days (how-to page) or 1-3 business days (FAQ and order form); and the how-to page and instruction sheet list card payments (the sheet adds Apple Pay, no American Express) while the FAQ and order form list only cash, check or money order. DFI's own pages also differ: 3-7 and 1-2 business days on its fee page, up to 7 and 2 business days or less in its FAQ. Call (608) 266-8888 or email Apostilles@wisconsin.gov to confirm.

name: Oregon
authority: Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division (authentications and apostilles)
fee_note: $10 per document (per apostille or authentication). You need a separate apostille for each notarized document, or, as the brochure puts it, for each original public official signature, but one request form can list several documents. Oregon uses the same certificate for apostilles and authentications, so the fee is the same for every country.
mail_time: The brochure says to allow 10 business days for regular mail; requests sent by FedEx or UPS (overnight or 2nd day) get priority handling and are processed within 2-3 business days. USPS Priority Mail and Express Mail get normal handling. The office's "Where's My Form?" box shows which receipt date it is working on: on 2026-11-24 it was processing apostille/authentication requests received 11/17/2026.
walkin_time: In-person counter at the Public Service Building, 255 Capitol St. NE, Suite 151, Salem, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday, excluding holidays. Arrive by 4:00 p.m. to ensure same-day processing; the office says some requests can take longer and can't be finished the same day. No appointment requirement is published, and there is no office in Portland.
payment: Check or money order, or credit card (Visa, MasterCard, Discover or American Express) entered on the request form. The request form (rev. 6/25) says to make checks payable to "Corporation Division"; the 2022 brochure says "State of Oregon". Cash is not accepted by mail. The official pages don't separately list which payment methods the walk-in counter takes.
addresses: Mail, FedEx/UPS and in person: Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division, Public Service Building, 255 Capitol St. NE, Suite 151, Salem, OR 97310-1327
phone: (503) 986-2200 (Contact Center: Monday-Thursday 8 a.m.-4:30 p.m., Friday 8 a.m.-12 p.m.); fax (503) 986-2300 (on the request form); email corporation.division@sos.oregon.gov (brochure) or the Corporation Division's online question form
what_to_send: The Request for Apostille/Authentication form (or a brief cover letter with your name, phone number and contact details), naming the destination country and listing each document and the names on it
Each original notarized document (with a complete Oregon notarial certificate) or original certified copy; photocopies are not accepted
$10 per document by check, money order or credit card

A self-addressed stamped envelope (large size, to avoid damage), or a prepaid, pre-printed FedEx or UPS label for express return (for international return, FedEx, UPS or DHL); or choose pick-up in person
tips: Can I get documents authenticated in Portland? No. The Secretary of State's office is in Salem; mail or deliver your request to the Corporation Division, 255 Capitol St. NE, Suite 151, Salem, OR 97310. Oregon Vital Records (Center for Health Statistics) is in Portland, at 800 N.E. Oregon St., Suite 205, but it issues the certified copies, not the apostille.

Vital records: get an original certified copy from the Oregon Center for Health Statistics or the Oregon county where the event took place (marriage and divorce certificates from the Center for Health Statistics). County copies must show the printed name of the certifying clerk. Oregon can only authenticate Oregon vital records. If you order through VitalChek you can ship the record straight to the Corporation Division and send the request form, fee and return envelope or label separately; the office matches them up.

School records: the registrar (or principal) must sign a statement on the transcript or diploma certifying it, in front of an Oregon notary who notarizes that statement. The brochure has sample wording and says the statement should go on the back or on a separate sheet stapled to the document, not on its face.

Background checks from the Oregon State Police or a local sheriff or police department must be signed by an official from that office and that signature notarized. Oregon cannot authenticate a records check obtained online or an FBI check (those go to the U.S. Department of State); don't send fingerprint cards.

Court and county documents (for example divorce decrees and name changes) must be original certified copies showing the official's signature, printed name and title. Business documents on file with the Corporation Division can be apostilled as certified copies; bylaws or minutes not on file must be notarized first.

Electronic or remote (RON) notarizations: the Secretary of State says it currently can't attach apostilles to electronic documents, but a printout can be apostilled if the notary completes and attaches a certificate for special circumstances.
Translations: the office doesn't translate. Get the translation done and notarized, then send it for the apostille. Don't remove an apostille once attached; removal invalidates it.
Don't use a hand-written prepaid shipping label or just a card or account number: the office can't use them and will return the documents by regular mail.

Official pages differ on a few details: the request form (rev. 6/25) says checks are payable to "Corporation Division" while the 2022 brochure says "State of Oregon"; the delivery-options page and request form accept FedEx, UPS or DHL labels for international return, but the how-to page and FAQ mention only FedEx and UPS; and the help box on the delivery-options page lists phone hours as Monday-Thursday 8 a.m.-4:30 p.m. without the Friday 8 a.m.-12 p.m. hours shown on the contact page. The office doesn't publish a regular-mail processing time on its web pages; the 10-business-day figure is from the 2022 brochure. Call (503) 986-2200 to confirm.
