Walk in by 4:00 p.m. (Monday-Friday) for same-day processing; FedEx or UPS requests are processed within 2-3 business days, and the brochure says to allow 10 business days for regular mail.

name: Nevada
authority: Nevada Secretary of State, Copies Division (apostilles and certifications)
fee_note: $20 per apostille or certification (Nevada issues an apostille for Hague Convention countries and a certification for non-Hague countries, at the same fee). Optional expedite fees are charged on top of the $20, per notary or official whose signature is authenticated: $75 for 24-hour, $125 for 4-hour, $500 for 2-hour and $1,000 for 1-hour service. Example from the fee schedule: one marriage certificate with 24-hour expedite = $95. Paying by credit card adds a non-refundable 2.5% processing fee.
mail_time: The official pages give different regular processing times: the main apostille page says "Standard processing time 2 weeks", the fee schedule page says regular processing is completed in approximately 4-6 weeks, and the order form (rev. 12/6/2024) says 4 weeks. On the Processing Dates page (last updated 11/24/2026) the office was processing apostille requests received 11/17/2026. Expedited requests are processed within the time frame selected (24, 4, 2 or 1 hour), counted from when the office receives the request in fileable form; the office can extend that if a signature can't be verified or during extreme volume. Mailing time is extra: documents are returned by First-Class Mail, even when expedited, unless you include a prepaid self-addressed envelope.
walkin_time: Carson City: the counter at the Paul Laxalt Building, 401 North Carson Street, accepts drop-off requests during hours of operation (walk-ins welcome), and Hold for Pick-Up orders can be collected there. Las Vegas: drop box at the Civic Center office, 70 E. Bonneville Ave., during regular business hours (drop boxes are picked up at 10:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m.; expedites start at those times); counter service is by appointment only, appointments are only offered for 1-hour or 2-hour expedited service, apostille pick-ups are only at the Civic Center office, and Las Vegas pick-up is only for expedited requests. The only faster turnaround the office publishes is paid expedite service (24, 4, 2 or 1 hour). The apostille pages don't list counter hours; customer service is Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-5 p.m.
payment: Check or money order payable to "The Office of the Secretary of State" (the main apostille page mentions only money order and card), or Visa, MasterCard, American Express or Discover using the ePayment Checklist (2.5% non-refundable card fee). The checklist says you can pay in person by cash, check or money order, but the contact page says cash is not accepted at the Las Vegas locations (credit card, check or money order only). Don't email the form or card details.
addresses: Mail and Carson City walk-in drop-off: Nevada Secretary of State, 401 North Carson St., Carson City, NV 89701 (Paul Laxalt Building)

Las Vegas (drop box; appointment-only counter for 1-hour/2-hour expedites; apostille pick-up for expedited requests): Nevada Secretary of State, 70 E. Bonneville Ave., Las Vegas, NV 89101 (Civic Center Plaza)
phone: 775-684-5708 (Copies Division / customer service, Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-5 p.m.); fax 775-684-5725; email sosmail@sos.nv.gov
what_to_send: One completed, printed and signed Apostille/Certification Order Form (rev. 12/6/2024). Unsigned forms are rejected, and requests without a destination country are not processed (if sending to a consulate, enter that consulate's country). Give an email address and a valid return address. One form can cover several documents.
The original document: a certified copy of the Nevada record (photocopies are rejected) or a document notarized by a Nevada notary. Send only the complete documents you want authenticated.
Payment of $20 per apostille/certification plus any expedite fee: a check or money order payable to "The Office of the Secretary of State", or the ePayment Checklist for a card

Optional: a prepaid, self-addressed return envelope or label if you want tracked or courier return; otherwise documents come back by First-Class Mail (the office says requests without shipping are returned by First-Class Mail International, without tracking)
tips: How many forms and envelopes do I need for several documents? The office says you may use one order form for multiple documents and must submit the form, payment and documents together. The fee is $20 for each apostille, so five birth certificates are five apostilles ($100). If you want tracked return, include one prepaid self-addressed envelope or label big enough for the whole order; the office doesn't say it needs one envelope per document.

Why is my Nevada apostille taking so long? The official pages quote 2 weeks (main page), 4 weeks (order form) or about 4-6 weeks (fee schedule) for regular service, plus mailing time. Check the Processing Dates page, which shows the receipt date the office is working on (11/17/2026 as of the 11/24/2026 update), and call 775-684-5708 if your request is older. Expedite fees ($75-$1,000) are the only published way to speed it up.

Vital records and court records: order the certified copy first. Birth certificates come from the state Office of Vital Records and Statistics; marriage certificates from the County Clerk's Office where the license was issued (the Secretary of State lists every county clerk and recorder); divorce decrees from the court that granted the divorce. Photocopies are rejected.
Documents filed with the Secretary of State's Commercial Recordings (business filings) follow a different procedure: call the Copies Division at 775-684-5708 for instructions before sending.

Shipping labels: labels marked "Bill to Sender" with the Secretary of State listed as the sender can't be used; use "Bill to Recipient" if applicable. A prepaid return label can show your own address as both sender and recipient. FedEx doesn't allow handwritten address information.
The office can't call international phone numbers, so give an email address on the form if you live abroad.
The apostille is stapled to the front of the page bearing the notary's or official's signature, with Nevada's red state stamp placed across both. Don't remove the staple.
Under NRS 240.1657 you sign a declaration on the form that the document won't be used for a fraudulent or unlawful purpose; the office can refuse documents that weren't notarized under Nevada law.

Official pages differ on a few details: regular processing time (2 weeks on the main page, 4 weeks on the order form, about 4-6 weeks on the fee schedule); payment (the main page lists money order and card, while the submission instructions also accept checks); and cash (the ePayment Checklist mentions paying cash in person, but the contact page says the Las Vegas locations don't take cash). The apostille pages don't say whether electronically or remotely notarized documents can be apostilled, and don't list counter hours. Call 775-684-5708 to confirm.

name: Utah
authority: Utah Office of the Lieutenant Governor, Authentications (apostilles and certificates of authentication)
fee_note: $5 per document for mail-in paper requests (not same-day), and $5 per adoption document. In-person, same-day service at an appointment costs $20 per document; if 2 or more documents are signed by the same public official or notary, each additional document after the first costs $5 ("Same Signer" fee). Example from the official FAQ: 3 documents presented in person, all signed by the same Utah notary = $20 + $5 + $5 = $30. Inter-governmental authentications cost $20 per document. Digital (electronic) certificates cost the $5 state fee plus a vendor charge, which the official pages state differently: $55 (FAQ and the Document Authentication page's "State Fees + $55" label; the FAQ and the in-person form give $60 per digital document in total) or $69.95 (a note on the same Document Authentication page, collected by the state's contracted provider). Utah issues one universal certificate that works as an apostille for Hague countries and as a certificate of authentication for other countries, at the same fee.
mail_time: Mail-in requests are processed within 1 to 3 business days from the date the office receives them; mailing time is extra, and USPS mail takes a couple of extra days because it goes through State Mail and a security check (the office suggests FedEx or UPS). Online orders (digital certificates) and in-person appointments are processed the same day. Documents are not processed on weekends or state and federal holidays, and the office says it offers no other expedited service. Mail-in requests must be started online first through the state's ApostilleXpress portal.
walkin_time: No walk-ins: in-person service at the Utah State Capitol, 350 North State Street, Suite 220, Salt Lake City, is by appointment only. Advance appointments open 2 weeks ahead; limited day-of appointments open at 10 a.m. each business day for same-day afternoon slots. Documents are ready about 10 to 15 minutes after your appointment time (the FAQ and the Document Authentication page differ) and up to 2 hours on busy days. Office hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., excluding state and federal holidays; the pages don't list appointment times.
payment: All major credit cards, checks or money orders payable to "State of Utah", or cash in person (the office strongly discourages mailing cash). Payment is due at the time of processing. Online orders are paid online; for mail-in, the Document Authentication page says to include a check, money order or card information on the form, while the FAQ and news pages describe paying online, so check which applies when you place the order.
addresses: In person (appointment only) and courier (UPS, FedEx): Office of the Lieutenant Governor, Utah State Capitol Building, 350 North State Street, Suite 220, Salt Lake City, UT 84114 (parking on the east side of the Capitol Hill complex)
USPS mail: Office of the Lieutenant Governor, PO Box 142325, Salt Lake City, UT 84114
Online (digital certificates, and the first step of every mail-in request): the state's contracted ApostilleXpress portal, apostille-xpress.com/utah
phone: 801-538-1041; fax 801-538-1133; email authentications@utah.gov (listed on the request form)
what_to_send: Mail-in: first submit your request online through ApostilleXpress (apostille-xpress.com/utah), then mail a printed copy of your online order delivery form

The original document(s): a certified copy issued by a Utah state agency, court or county clerk (for example a birth certificate from Vital Records or a divorce decree from the District Court Clerk), or a document properly notarized by a Utah notary with a complete notarial certificate
Payment of $5 per document (check or money order payable to "State of Utah", or card information on the form, per the Document Authentication page)

A self-addressed return envelope, ideally prepaid with tracking; without a prepaid label the office returns documents by USPS First Class Mail with no tracking. Mailed documents can't be picked up in person, and the office drop box has been discontinued.

In person (appointment only): bring the In-Person Document Authentication Request Form, completely filled out before your appointment, with the original documents and payment ($20 per document, $5 per additional same-signer document)
tips: Do I need an appointment in Utah? Yes. The official FAQ says the office does not accept walk-ins. Book up to 2 weeks ahead, try the limited day-of slots that open at 10 a.m. each business day, or order online instead. Arrive with the paper form completely filled out, or other appointments may be processed ahead of yours.

Utah business documents (for example a Certificate of Existence): the document must be a certified copy from the Utah Department of Commerce and notarized at the Department. Emailed or printed copies are not accepted. Then submit it to the Lieutenant Governor's office.

Digital (e-Apostille) option: since September 3, 2026 you can order online and receive the certificate by email, verifiable on the state's e-Register (verifyapostille.utah.gov). Digital certificates are not available for birth or death certificates or anything issued by the Utah Division of Vital Records and Statistics. Check that your destination authority accepts digital apostilles before ordering.

Power of attorney: the office authenticates it only if the notary does not attest to the contents of the document (unless the notary is also a licensed attorney). The office can't notarize and authenticate in the same visit, and doesn't translate documents.

Utah only authenticates Utah documents and Utah notarizations. FBI background checks and other federal documents go to the U.S. Department of State; federal court documents are authenticated by the federal court that issued them.

Official pages differ on a few details: the digital vendor charge ($55 on top of the $5 state fee, i.e. $60 per document, in the FAQ, on the Document Authentication page and on the in-person form, but $69.95 in a separate note on the Document Authentication page); how soon in-person documents are ready (10 minutes in the FAQ, 15 minutes on the Document Authentication page, up to 2 hours on both); how mail-in requests are paid (check or card information on the form vs paying online); and walk-ins (the address section is labelled "Walk-ins & Physical Address", but the FAQ says walk-ins are not accepted). The Contact Us page still shows an older closure list than the home page. The pages don't say whether electronically or remotely notarized documents can be authenticated. Call 801-538-1041 to confirm.
